Food calories

How many calories in ramen?

Ramen: about 500 kcal per serving (1 bowl, 500 g). That serving has 24 g protein, 60 g carbs and 18 g fat, which works out to about 100 kcal per 100 g.

Calories and nutrition

Per serving (1 bowl, 500 g)Per 100 g
Calories500 kcal100 kcal
Protein24 g4.8 g
Carbohydrates60 g12 g
Fat18 g3.6 g

Smaller or larger portion

PortionCaloriesProtein
Half a portion (250 g)250 kcal12 g
Typical portion (500 g)500 kcal24 g
One and a half portions (750 g)750 kcal36 g

Where the calories come from

19% of the calories come from protein, 48% from carbohydrates and 33% from fat. In short: a mix of protein, carbohydrates and fat.

One portion is about 25% of a 2,000 kcal day, the reference value used on food labels.

Why the number varies

Home and restaurant recipes differ in the amount of oil, meat, cheese and starch, and in portion size. Treat the value as a starting point and adjust the serving if your plate was smaller or larger.

How to log it in Pofu

Pofu is our app. To log this food, take a photo of your plate: Pofu estimates the food and portion and shows a confidence score, so you can see how sure it is and correct it. You can also search by name or scan a barcode, then set the serving to match what you ate. Get Pofu on the App Store.

Questions about this food

Ramen: how many calories are in 100 g?

About 100 kcal per 100 g, with 4.8 g of protein, 12 g of carbohydrates and 3.6 g of fat.

Ramen: is it high in protein?

It has some protein: 24 g per portion, about 19% of its calories.

Ramen: how do I log it in Pofu?

Take a photo of your plate or search for the name, then set the portion to what you actually ate. You can correct the estimate, and Pofu remembers your correction next time.

Values: typical estimates used in the Pofu app; they vary by recipe and portion. How we prepare our content and sources.

This page is general information, not medical advice. If you are pregnant, breastfeeding, have a medical condition or a history of an eating disorder, talk to your doctor or dietitian before counting calories.
